paras: The killing of George Engart was the death of a man at a dance at Roanoke, Missouri, on the night of Saturday, January 29, 1881, at the hands of a deputy constable, Add Cross. Known only from a one-sentence St. Louis wire dispatch, the killing ran as a crime brief in papers from West Virginia to California in early February.

According to the dispatch, a "row" broke out at what the papers called "a negro dance" at Roanoke on Saturday night. During the row, Engart was killed by Add Cross, described as "a deputy constable"; only the Wheeling Register's version says he was "shot and killed." A Montana weekly gave the date as "the 29th, ult.," which matches the Saturday in the other versions. The papers do not give Engart's race, the cause of the row, or whether Cross was trying to make an arrest.
No report of an arrest, inquest or charge against Cross appears in the coverage.

The item was a St. Louis dispatch dated February 3, and it appeared that day in the Press and Daily Dakotaian under "Killed at a Dance" and in the Rock Island Argus. On February 4 it ran in the Sacramento Daily Record-Union as "Homicide at a Ball," in the Salt Lake Herald's "Criminal Calendar," and in shortened form in the Cheyenne Daily Leader. The Weekly Miner of Butte, Montana, reworded it in a news digest on February 8.

Spellings of the victim's name varied from paper to paper, including Engart, Engeart, Enycart and Enickart. None of the papers commented on the killing; their only racial term was the label "negro dance." The Wheeling Register printed the item under the heading "Narrow Escape From a Mob," but that heading belonged to the next paragraph on the page, about soldiers at Fort Concho, Texas, who had tried to lynch a man named McCarthy. No Missouri paper's account of the killing was found.

bases: Every version says a deputy constable, Add Cross, killed George Engart during a row at a dance, and none mentions a mob or crowd taking part (A1, A6, A7).
All seven items are versions of one St. Louis wire dispatch of February 3 (A1, A4, A6); no local Missouri report, inquest or second account was found.

accounts.label: St. Louis wire report
accounts.gist: During a row at a negro dance at Roanoke, Mo., on Saturday night, George Engart was killed (shot, in one version) by Add Cross, a deputy constable; nothing is said about the cause of the row or what followed.

framing.detail: Papers ran the dispatch as a one-line crime brief ('Killed at a Dance', 'Homicide at a Ball', 'The Criminal Calendar') with no comment beyond calling the dance a 'negro dance'.
The Wheeling Register printed the item under the head 'Narrow Escape From a Mob', a head that belongs to the Fort Concho story set right after it.

conflicts.note: Telegraphic variants of one name; the correct spelling cannot be settled from the coverage.
Not a contradiction; only the Wheeling text names the weapon.

record_check.record: the item's headline reports a narrow escape from a mob. The text is truncated and the mob's actions are not reported.
record_check.dossier: The Wheeling text is complete. Its head 'Narrow Escape From a Mob' covers the Fort Concho, Tex., item printed after it, where soldiers tried to lynch McCarthy; no mob took part at Roanoke.
George Engart (also spelled Engeart, Enycart, Enickart); no spelling is authoritative.
No county is named in any paper; only 'Roanoke, Mo.'
Not stated; the papers say only that it was a 'negro dance'.
